evidence: Film morphology was studied with scanning electron microscopy (SEM, Hitachi S-4800) and atomic force microscopy (AFM, Veeco Multimode V). AFM imaging was performed in ambient air in tapping mode (intermittent contact mode), using silicon probes (Bruker) with a tip radius of less than 10 nm. Film thicknesses were measured by energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX, Oxford INCA 350 connected to the Hitachi S4800 SEM) and time-of-flight elastic recoil detection analysis (TOF-ERDA). Conformality was estimated using optical microscope (Olympus BX 51), and film thicknesses were measured by SEM cross-section imaging as well as EDX line scans. Cross-sectional SEM is probably the most widely used method for film conformality analysis.
